summary: The 1867 granite light on Sandy Point, Block Island's northern tip, fourth on the point; kept by civilians and Coast Guard until 1955 and now a museum on its ground floor.

lens.note: Kerosene Fresnel lantern built in Paris; the French lenses remained when the 1973 nomination was written (NRHP)

structures.note: Main block 30 by 33 ft of 18-inch granite; the iron tower rises over the central entrance (NRHP)

access.note: First floor open as a maritime museum, Saturday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. and Sunday noon to 4 p.m. in season; no tower access. Closed for the season after Columbus Day and in rain.

facts.agency: Town of New Shoreham (North Light Commission)

events.note: First tower on Sandy Point, 45 ft high (NRHP). The record and USLHS date the first light to 1829.
Hiram D. Ball appointed by President Lincoln; kept the light until 1891
Present granite tower completed; the fourth light on the point (Town of New Shoreham)
Renamed North Light from Sandy Point Light when the South East Light was completed
Coast Guard maintenance ends; the structure is automated (NRHP)
Abandoned as an active light station (NRHP). The archive gives 1970-1989 as its discontinuance years.
North Light Commission established by the Town Council, 30 December 1974
Relighting ceremony, 23 October 2010, marks completion of the tower and roof restoration

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination says a lighthouse was first erected on the point in 1827; the USLHS record gives 1829 as the year the station was established. Both are given in the story and the disagreement is stated, not resolved.

resolved_conflicts.field: end of Coast Guard service and abandonment
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The nomination says the Coast Guard kept the light until automation in 1955 and that it was abandoned from 1970. The USLHS record gives 1970-1989 as its discontinuance years, and the station record gives 1973 as the deactivation year. The story uses the nomination and gives the archive's range.
The nomination's 13.5 statute miles is about 11.7 nautical miles (converted here); the station record gives 11 nautical miles. The two figures are close and differ in units and method.

notes_for_editor: The NRHP nomination was read in full (OCR; the 1884 quotation is Pettee, Block Island, as quoted in the nomination, and is footnoted that way). The owner's name in the nomination is a federal agency; no private owners are named. The roster's 'Principal Lighthouse Keeper' lines are normalised to head keeper; roster.py prints the same names and person slugs. The contractor lines (David Melville, John Stevens) carry no dates and are not linked to any work. The 1921 Commissioner entry is in the Third District list of the summary of work completed in fiscal year 1921. It is read from running text, not matched by column position. Its printed page is 53: the page header '53' opens the page with the summary, and the page header '54' opens the next page after it. The 1898 Life-Saving passage is on printed page 43 (header 43 opens the page, header 44 opens the next). Do not use the 1930 Bulletin passage about electrifying 'Sandy Point Light Station' (fourth-order lens, Fort Howard context): it is Sandy Point Shoal Light in Maryland, a different station. The 1927 Bulletin's Sandy Point, Connecticut and the 1923 Block Island North gas buoy are also different aids. The USLHS record shows 'Active Aid to Navigation?: Yes' and 'Current Optic: DCB-24', which conflicts with the nomination's account of abandonment in 1970; the story states the archive's entry. Whether the lamp is lit today is not stated in the sources read; the Town's 2010 relighting ceremony is the only later evidence of a lit light. The USLHS place page gives coordinates 41 deg 13.8 min N, 71 deg 13.8 min W, which place the station about 29 km from its true position; the record's OSM coordinates are right and are not changed. No wreck, storm or rescue at this light is dated in the corpus or in the sources read; the 1898 Life-Saving report is about the separate Sandy Point station. The Town's 'Lighthouse Bureau' wording is not used: the Bureau did not exist in 1867 (it was the Light-House Board). The record's NRHP listing year (1974) was not verified against the nomination's stamped page. The Town's hours and admission should be checked before a visit.
